title: Your trading results are stuck, but it's not why you think

channel.name: Andrew Builds (TradeNotes)
channel.appBlurb: a trading journal and performance analytics app

body.hook: Your trading results are stuck. But it's not why you think.
body.promise: Three things hide in every plateau. The third, almost nobody writes down.

beats.narration: Number one: the result. But profit and loss only says what happened, never why.

scene.caption: #1 The result: what happened, never why

beats.narration: Number two: the plan. Setup, risk, exit, written before the trade. Still, one piece is missing.

scene.label: #2 Before the trade
scene.text: Setup: pullback. Risk: 1R. Stop: below the low. Exit: target or stop.
scene.caption: One piece is still missing...

beats.narration: Number three: what you actually did. Moved the stop. Sized up after a loss. Almost nobody logs that.
Here is what surprised me. Line up all three, and a plateau can stop looking like bad luck. It looks like one habit, repeated.

scene.title: Plan vs. actual
scene.note: 45 SAMPLE trades. 23 broke the plan. Illustration only, not real results.

cards.label: Moved the stop
cards.hint: The same habit, again and again.

beats.narration: I built TradeNotes, my own trading journal, so I'm biased. It keeps all three side by side.
So maybe you are not stuck on effort. You are stuck on measurement. No journal removes the risk of loss. It shows your own behavior.

scene.sub: You can't fix a habit you never recorded.

body.cta: Tonight, log one thing on your last trade: what you actually did. Not financial advice.

cta.title: TradeNotes
cta.tagline: Journal the plan, the action and the result. Next: the plan-versus-actual gap.

post.ytTitle: Your trading is stuck. It's not why you think.
post.ytDesc: Most trading journals record one thing: the result. This short walks through the three things worth writing down for every trade (the plan, what you actually did, and the result) and why a plateau can be a measurement problem rather than an effort problem. The numbers on screen are SAMPLE data, not real trades. A journal does not improve results by itself and cannot remove the risk of loss; it gives you evidence about your own behavior. I built TradeNotes, so I'm biased. Part 1 of 5. Educational content only, not financial advice.
